# Vamsa

A modern family tree management application built with Next.js 15, focusing on privacy-first local storage with optional cloud sync.

## Features

- **Privacy First**: All data stored locally by default using SQLite
- **Modern Stack**: Next.js 15, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS
- **Family Management**: Create and manage multiple family trees
- **Member Profiles**: Track names, birthdates, and relationships
- **Relationship Mapping**: Visual family tree with parent-child and spouse connections
- **Data Portability**: Export/import family data in standard GEDCOM format
- **Backup System**: Create and restore backups of your family data
- **Google Authentication**: Sign in with Google to associate your family trees

## Tech Stack

- **Framework**: Next.js 15 (App Router)
- **Database**: SQLite with Prisma ORM
- **Authentication**: NextAuth.js with Google OAuth
- **UI**: Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui components
- **Visualization**: React Flow for family tree rendering
- **Testing**: Vitest for unit tests, Playwright for e2e tests

## Getting Started

### Prerequisites

- Node.js 18+
- Google OAuth credentials (for authentication)

### Setup

1. Clone the repository
2. Install dependencies:
   ```bash
   npm install
   ```
3. Copy the environment file and configure:
   ```bash
   cp .env.example .env.local
   ```
4. Add your Google OAuth credentials to `.env.local`
5. Initialize the database:
   ```bash
   npx prisma generate
   npx prisma db push
   ```
6. Start the development server:
   ```bash
   npm run dev
   ```

## Project Structure

```
src/
├── actions/          # Server actions for data operations
├── app/              # Next.js app router pages
├── components/       # React components
├── lib/              # Utility libraries
│   ├── backup/       # Backup/restore functionality
│   ├── gedcom/       # GEDCOM import/export
│   ├── storage/      # Storage abstraction
│   └── utils.ts      # General utilities
└── types/            # TypeScript type definitions
```

## Data Model

- **Family**: A family tree container
- **Person**: Individual family members with names and birthdates
- **Relationship**: Connections between people (parent-child, spouse)

## Privacy

Vamsa is designed with privacy as a core principle:

- All data is stored locally in SQLite
- No data is sent to external servers (except for authentication)
- Google sign-in is optional and only used for user identification
- Full data export capability ensures you always own your data

## License

generator client {
  provider = "prisma-client-js"
}

datasource db {
  provider = "sqlite"
  url      = env("DATABASE_URL")
}

model Account {
  id                String  @id @default(cuid())
  userId            String
  type              String
  provider          String
  providerAccountId String
  refresh_token     String?
  access_token      String?
  expires_at        Int?
  token_type        String?
  scope             String?
  id_token          String?
  session_state     String?

  user User @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([provider, providerAccountId])
}

model Session {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  sessionToken String   @unique
  userId       String
  expires      DateTime
  user         User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
}

model User {
  id            String    @id @default(cuid())
  name          String?
  email         String?   @unique
  emailVerified DateTime?
  image         String?
  accounts      Account[]
  sessions      Session[]
  families      Family[]
}

model VerificationToken {
  identifier String
  token      String   @unique
  expires    DateTime

  @@unique([identifier, token])
}

model Family {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  name        String
  description String?
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
  userId      String
  user        User     @relation(fields: [userId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  members     Person[]
  sources     Source[]
  media       Media[]
}

model Person {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  firstName    String
  lastName     String?
  birthDate    String?
  deathDate    String?
  gender       String?
  notes        String?
  createdAt    DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt    DateTime @updatedAt
  familyId     String
  family       Family   @relation(fields: [familyId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  gedcomId     String?
  birthPlace   String?
  deathPlace   String?
  occupation   String?
  sourceCitations SourceCitation[]
  mediaLinks      MediaLink[]

  // Relationships where this person is the subject
  relationshipsAsSubject Relationship[] @relation("SubjectPerson")
  // Relationships where this person is the relative
  relationshipsAsRelative Relationship[] @relation("RelativePerson")
}

model Relationship {
  id         String   @id @default(cuid())
  type       String // "parent", "child", "spouse"
  subjectId  String
  relativeId String
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now())

  subject  Person @relation("SubjectPerson", fields: [subjectId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  relative Person @relation("RelativePerson", fields: [relativeId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)

  @@unique([subjectId, relativeId, type])
}

model Source {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  familyId    String
  family      Family   @relation(fields: [familyId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  gedcomId    String?
  title       String?
  author      String?
  publisher   String?
  publication String?
  repository  String?
  callNumber  String?
  text        String?
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
  citations   SourceCitation[]

  @@index([familyId])
  @@index([gedcomId])
}

model SourceCitation {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  sourceId  String
  source    Source   @relation(fields: [sourceId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  personId  String
  person    Person   @relation(fields: [personId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  page      String?
  quality   String?
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([sourceId])
  @@index([personId])
}

model Media {
  id          String   @id @default(cuid())
  familyId    String
  family      Family   @relation(fields: [familyId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  gedcomId    String?
  filePath    String?
  format      String?
  title       String?
  createdAt   DateTime @default(now())
  updatedAt   DateTime @updatedAt
  links       MediaLink[]

  @@index([familyId])
  @@index([gedcomId])
}

model MediaLink {
  id        String   @id @default(cuid())
  mediaId   String
  media     Media    @relation(fields: [mediaId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  personId  String
  person    Person   @relation(fields: [personId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now())

  @@index([mediaId])
  @@index([personId])
}

## Codebase Summary: Vamsa

**Vamsa** is a modern, privacy-first family tree management application built with Next.js 15 and React 19.

### Key Technologies
- **Framework**: Next.js 15 with App Router
- **Runtime**: Bun (for scripts and testing)
- **Database**: SQLite with Prisma ORM
- **Authentication**: NextAuth.js with Google OAuth
- **UI**: Tailwind CSS v4 + shadcn/ui + Radix primitives
- **Visualization**: React Flow (@xyflow/react) for family tree rendering
- **Testing**: Bun test runner (unit tests), Playwright (e2e tests)

### Project Structure
```
src/
├── actions/          # Server actions (backup, family, person CRUD)
├── app/              # Next.js app router pages
│   ├── api/          # API routes (auth, backup, GEDCOM import/export)
│   ├── family/[id]/  # Family tree view pages
│   └── settings/     # Settings page with data management
├── components/       # React components (auth, family, layout, UI)
├── lib/              # Core libraries
│   ├── backup/       # Backup/restore with conflict resolution
│   ├── gedcom/       # GEDCOM file import/export parsing
│   ├── storage/      # Storage abstraction layer
│   └── utils.ts      # General utilities
└── types/            # TypeScript definitions
```

### Data Model (Prisma/SQLite)
- **User** - Google OAuth user accounts
- **Family** - Family tree containers owned by users
- **Person** - Individual family members with biographical data
- **Relationship** - Parent-child and spouse connections
- **Source** - Citation sources for genealogical data
- **SourceCitation** - Links between sources and people
- **Media** - Multimedia objects (photos, documents)
- **MediaLink** - Links between media and people

### Current Work in Progress
Based on git status, GEDCOM Phase 2 is being implemented with:
- Source and Media model additions
- GEDCOM encoding support (ANSEL)
- Object/multimedia parsing and mapping
- Source parsing and mapping
- GEDCOM 7.0 support

### Critical Files for Implementation
- `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/vamsa/prisma/schema.prisma` - Core data model
- `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/vamsa/src/lib/gedcom/parser.ts` - GEDCOM parsing logic
- `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/vamsa/src/actions/person.ts` - Person CRUD operations
- `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/vamsa/src/app/family/[id]/components/family-tree-view.tsx` - Tree visualization
- `/Users/rambhiad/Code/Repositories/personal-projects/vamsa/src/lib/backup/conflict-resolver.test.ts` - Backup/sync patterns
